title: Running AI Application in Minutes w/ AI Templates: Gabriela de Queiroz, Pamela Fox, Harald Kirschner
talk_summary: A Microsoft workshop demoing three Azure AI app templates (chat, RAG-on-Postgres, RAG-on-documents) deployed via GitHub Codespaces and azd/bicep, aimed at getting startups to a running app in minutes. Most content is Azure onboarding and template plumbing, but a few concrete engineering lessons on retrieval, chunking, and evaluation leak out in the Q&A.

takeaways.technique: Tiered eval sets gated on PRs plus daily full runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Copilot Chat runs a small unit-test-style eval subset on every PR (regressions they've seen before) and a much larger cross-language set daily; evals are cached and only rerun when inputs/prompts change because they are slow and expensive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a one test set that can run on each PR and then a larger test set that we run daily

takeaways.technique: Cheap regex metric over LLM-judge metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Alongside GPT-scored groundedness/relevance they track a citation-match metric implemented as a plain regex against ground truth, which the speaker calls her favorite because it's cheap and stable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that's actually my favorite metric and that's just a Rex

takeaways.what_they_do: They chunk documents by tokens (~500) rather than characters because character splits blow past context windows on non-English/CJK text; they cite 512 tokens as the researched optimum.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you really want to do stuff based off of tokens and not characters

takeaways.what_they_do: She reports prompt engineering never moved eval numbers, while changing retrieval (text vs vector vs hybrid vs semantic rerank, top-k) and swapping the model did; vector-only scored far worse than full-text.
takeaways.evidence_quote: none of my prompt engineering ever moves a needle for me the only thing that moves a needle is retrieval parameters
takeaways.numbers: vector-only groundedness 2.79 vs text-only 4.87; hybrid 3.26; hybrid+semantic ranker best

takeaways.what_they_do: Copilot Chat chunks code by function/block segments rather than fixed windows, which they call the biggest impact area, and reranks with an LLM call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually do schematic chunking so for most languages we look at function segments

takeaways.technique: Small models for narrow subtasks, not full answers
takeaways.what_they_do: Small local models failed at full RAG (bad citation formatting, hallucination) but were judged useful for reranking/judging single narrow decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: good for reranking I think ... that's where like finding this one thing maybe not like the expert full answers
